messages:
maria_support: forwarding a customer escalation — they hit a 422 on function output validation. Request-id in customer response: rdx-1790012345-abc123. Can someone triage?

ryan_engineer: On it. Need the exact curl they used and the raw HTTP response body + headers to repro.

maria_support: Customer pasted this curl (api key redacted):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{
    \"model\":\"open-variant-3b\",
    \"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"List onboarding steps\"}],
    \"functions\":[{\n      \"name\":\"onboard_steps\",\n      \"parameters\":{\n        \"type\":\"object\",\n        \"properties\":{\n          \"steps\":{\"type\":\"array\",\"items\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}\n        },\n        \"required\":[\"steps\"]\n      }\n    }],
    \"function_call\":\"auto\"\n  }'
```

And the HTTP response they pasted: 

```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
Content-Type: application/json
x-request-id: rdx-1790012345-abc123

{\"error\":{\"message\":\"Schema validation failed: unexpected property 'tasks' in function result\",\"type\":\"invalid_output\"},\"request_id\":\"rdx-1790012345-abc123\"}
```

maria_support: They also uploaded a debug bundle after we asked them to rerun with X-Debug: true. Support link: https://s3.redwood.ai/support/bundles/bundle-1790012345-abc123.tar.gz

sam_ops: I fetched the bundle and extracted the runtime log. The recorded function result object we received (trimmed) looks like:

```
{\"name\":\"onboard_steps\",\"arguments\":\"{\\\"tasks\\\": [\\\"Sign up\\\", \\\"Confirm email\\\", \\\"Set up profile\\\"] }\"}
```

ryan_engineer: That matches the 422 — model returned 'tasks' inside the serialized arguments string but the schema strictly requires 'steps'. Server validation parses the arguments string into JSON then compares the keys; mismatch yields 422.

anika_ml: This is model output variance. Models can emit synonyms. For immediate repro I sent a local request with the same payload and the same model — it returned 'tasks' consistently in a couple trials.

ryan_engineer: Notes for support reply: 1) This is not a server bug — validation behaved as designed. 2) Attach the debug bundle link and the offending JSON snippet. 3) Short-term workarounds: update schema to accept additionalProperties or accept/normalize 'tasks' client-side; add an explicit system instruction to force exact key names. 4) Long-term: consider UX features like a lenient_validation flag or a validation hint in the API.

anika_ml: Suggested system instruction for docs/examples: \"System: When invoking the function 'onboard_steps', return exactly a JSON object with a top-level key named 'steps' containing an array of strings. Do not use synonyms like 'tasks' or 'actions'.\"

maria_support: Customer asked whether Redwood can automatically map common synonyms for them. They said they have a production workload and changing client parsing is a risk.

sam_ops: Operational caution — accepting synonyms server-side could mask schema bugs and cause downstream processing problems. If customer needs immediate relief, recommend: 1) client-side normalization (map 'tasks' -> 'steps'), or 2) add 'additionalProperties: true' to the function parameters temporarily.

ryan_engineer: I'll open an internal engineering ticket for a nicer error message and a possible opt-in lenient mode. For the support reply, here's a draft they can copy: 

\"Thanks — we confirmed the cause. The model returned a payload with key 'tasks' while your declared function schema expects 'steps', and the platform correctly rejected that output, resulting in a 422. We attached the debug bundle for the exact server-side capture: https://s3.redwood.ai/support/bundles/bundle-1790012345-abc123.tar.gz. Workarounds: (A) Update your parsing to map 'tasks' -> 'steps' or accept both keys; (B) Temporarily set 'additionalProperties: true' in the function schema; (C) Add a system instruction to your conversation to force the model to use the exact key name. We are also evaluating an opt-in lenient_validation feature to reduce these breaks — I'll update you if that ships.\"

maria_support: Sent to customer. They replied: \"Thanks, trying the system instruction now. Will confirm shortly.\" Ticket SR-3245 opened, severity low, engineering ETA TBD.

sam_ops: Note: debug bundle will be retained for 7 days; archived copy: https://s3.redwood.ai/support/archives/arch-1790012345-abc123.tar.gz

maria_support: Leaving thread open until they confirm resolution. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
